title: Buttons
subtitle: A row of one or more links styled as buttons, for the next thing a reader should do.

tutorial.p: Buttons holds a row of one or more Button blocks. Each button is a link: its label is the text the reader sees, and its address is where it goes. Use it for the action a reader should take next, such as reading on, signing up or getting in touch.

No template or template part on this site uses Buttons, so a row appears only where an editor adds one. Many of the theme's patterns hold one, among them Centered heading, Newsletter sign-up and Pricing, 2 columns.

steps.text: Open the + (block inserter) at the top left, type buttons in the search field and click Buttons.
steps.alt: The block inserter searched for buttons, with the Buttons tile outlined in red

steps.text: Or type /buttons in an empty paragraph and choose Buttons from the list.
steps.alt: An empty paragraph reading /buttons, with the list of matching blocks below it

steps.text: A row with one button appears, reading Add text…. Click the button and type its label.
steps.alt: A Buttons row just added, with one button reading Add text… and the button's toolbar above it

steps.text: Save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.p: A button with a label and no address still shows on the site, and does nothing when clicked.

steps.text: With the button selected, click Link in the toolbar, type the address and press Enter. The link appears under the field.
steps.alt: The link popup under a button reading Read the guide, showing wordpress.org with the Edit link, Remove link and Copy link icons

steps.text: To open it in a new tab, click the pencil icon (Edit link). Open Advanced if it is closed, tick Open in new tab and click Apply.
steps.alt: The link field open for editing, with Open in new tab ticked under Advanced, and the Cancel and Apply buttons

tutorial.h3: Adding another button to the row

tutorial.p: The + at the end of the row adds a button beside the others. It shows only while the row is selected. From a button, click Select parent block: Buttons, the first item in its toolbar, to select the row.

images.alt: A selected Buttons row with one button and a + at its right end
images.caption: The + at the end of the selected row.

images.alt: The same row after clicking the +, now holding two buttons that read Add text…
images.caption: After clicking it, a second button.

steps.text: With a button selected, the sidebar's Styles panel offers Fill, a solid button, and Outline, a button with a border and no fill. Each button in a row takes its own style.
steps.alt: The sidebar for a Button, with the Styles panel offering Fill, which is selected, and Outline

steps.text: With the row selected, Change items justification in the toolbar sets the buttons to the left, the centre or the right, or spreads them across the row.
steps.alt: The list Change items justification opened from the row's toolbar: Justify items left, Justify items center, Justify items right and Space between items

steps.text: Save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.p: A pattern adds blocks with sample text already in them. The theme's Centered heading pattern adds a centred heading, a line of text and a Learn more button. Start from it for a band like that, keeping its layout and amount of text. To decide the layout yourself, add Buttons on its own as above.

Clicking a band added from a pattern selects the whole pattern, and its blocks cannot be changed as they are. To change its text or button, click Edit pattern, and click Exit pattern when you finish. The change applies to this page only.

steps.text: In the + (block inserter) at the top left, open the Patterns tab and type centered heading in the search field. Click the first preview, Centered heading.
steps.alt: The block inserter's Patterns tab searched for centered heading, with the Centered heading preview first and Simple call to action beside it

steps.text: Click the band that was added, and the sidebar shows the pattern's name and description. Click Edit pattern. The bar at the top then reads "Back Centered heading · Pattern", and the button can be changed.
steps.alt: The sidebar with the Centered heading pattern selected: its name, its description and the Edit pattern button

steps.text: When you finish, click Exit pattern and save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.p: Button only. A Button cannot be added on its own: it always sits in a Buttons row.

checklist_intro.p: Tickets: none. This is a demonstration checklist for core's Buttons block on Twenty Twenty-Five.

steps.step: Add the block and save it
steps.alt: The link field open for editing, with Open in new tab ticked under Advanced, and the Cancel and Apply buttons
instructions: Create a new page and close Choose a pattern.
Type a label in the button.
Tick Open in new tab (pencil icon → Advanced) and click Apply.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
expected: After Apply, the link popup shows the address with a ↗ beside it.
After the reload your label is still there, with no "Block contains unexpected or invalid content." message.

steps.step: Add a second button and change the style
steps.alt: A selected Buttons row with one button and a + at its right end
instructions: In the same draft, click Select parent block: Buttons in the button's toolbar.
Click the + at the end of the row and type a label in the new button.
Select the row again and choose Justify items center from Change items justification.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
expected: The second button has a border and no fill, and the first keeps its fill.
Both buttons sit in the centre of the row.
After the reload every change is still there.

steps.alt: The sidebar with the Centered heading pattern selected: its name, its description and the Edit pattern button
instructions: Create a new page and close Choose a pattern.
In the Patterns tab of +, search for centered heading and add Centered heading.
Click Edit pattern, change the button's label, then click Exit pattern.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
expected: A band with the heading Tell your story, a line of text and a Learn more button is added.
After the reload the new label is still there, with no "Block contains unexpected or invalid content." message.

checklist.section: Front end at desktop width (a full-width laptop or desktop window)

steps.step: Preview the draft from the second step (laptop icon at the top right → Preview in new tab).
steps.expected: The two buttons sit side by side in the centre, the second with a border and no fill.

steps.step: Compare the examples on this page with the desktop design.
steps.expected: Colours, fonts, corners and spacing match the design.

steps.step: Click Read the guide in the first example on this page.
steps.expected: The home page opens in the same tab.

steps.step: Click Visit WordPress.org in the examples on this page.
steps.expected: WordPress.org opens in a new tab.

steps.step: View the examples on this page.
steps.expected: Every button shows in full, and the page does not scroll sideways.

steps.step: Compare the examples with the mobile design.
steps.expected: Colours, fonts, corners and spacing match the design.

steps.step: Look at the example with the long label.
steps.expected: The label wraps inside the button, with no text cut off.

steps.step: Press Tab until Read the guide in the first example is selected, then press Enter.
steps.expected: The button shows a focus outline, and Enter opens the home page.

steps.expected: Nothing overlaps or is cut off.
